model_family: Whirlpool WED5050LW 7.0 cu. ft. electric dryer
sticker_location: Open the dryer door and look on the frame around the door opening. The white sticker there shows the model number (WED5050LW) and serial number.

parts.label: lint screen
parts.where: On top of the dryer, near the back. Pull it straight up to take it out.

parts.label: lint screen slot
parts.where: The narrow opening on top of the dryer where the lint screen slides in.

parts.label: cycle knob
parts.where: The big turning knob on the control panel at the top back of the dryer.

parts.label: power button
parts.where: On the control panel at the top back of the dryer. It turns the dryer on or off.

parts.label: start button
parts.where: On the control panel, marked Start/Pause. Press and hold it to start.

parts.label: temperature button
parts.where: On the control panel, marked Temp. It changes how hot the air gets.

parts.label: options button
parts.where: On the control panel, marked Options. It turns on extra help like Wrinkle Shield.

parts.label: dryer door
parts.where: The big door on the front of the dryer that opens to the round tub inside.

parts.label: door latch
parts.where: The catch on the dryer door that clicks shut when you push the door closed.

parts.label: dryer drum
parts.where: The big round tub inside the dryer where clothes tumble.

parts.label: moisture sensor strips
parts.where: Two shiny metal strips just inside the drum, near the door opening. They feel how wet the clothes are.

parts.label: drum light bulb
parts.where: Behind a small cover on the back wall inside the drum, seen when you open the door.

parts.label: drying rack
parts.where: A flat rack that sits still inside the drum for shoes or sweaters, if your dryer has one.

parts.label: outside vent hood
parts.where: The flap on the outside wall of your home where warm air blows out.

parts.label: vent hose
parts.where: The wide silver tube behind the dryer that carries warm air to the outside.

parts.label: leveling feet
parts.where: Four small feet at the bottom corners of the dryer that twist up or down.

parts.label: power plug
parts.where: The big plug on the cord behind the dryer, in the wall outlet.

parts.label: home breaker box
parts.where: Your home's breaker box, often in the garage, basement, or a utility closet. This dryer uses two breakers.

parts.label: water inlet hose
parts.where: On steam models, the water hose connected to the back of the dryer.

symptoms: My clothes are still damp after a full cycle
It takes two runs to dry towels
The dryer runs forever and clothes feel warm but wet

plan.diagnosis: Your lint screen is choking the airflow. Hot air has to pass through it to leave the drum, so a clogged screen traps moist air and the clothes stay damp. A blocked outside vent or an overfull drum does the same.
safety: Clean the lint screen before every load.
Do not run the dryer with the lint screen loose, damaged, or missing.
If the vent inside the wall needs cleaning, have a qualified vent cleaner do it.

steps.instruction: See where the hot air gets stuck
details: Hot air leaves the drum through the lint screen.
A full screen chokes it, so clothes stay damp.
steps.check: You know the air has to get through the lint screen.

steps.instruction: Pull the lint screen straight up
details: It is on top of the dryer, near the back.
steps.check: The lint screen is fully out of its slot.

steps.instruction: Roll lint off screen with fingers
details: Do not wash it for this quick clean.
Wet lint is hard to remove.
steps.check: You can see through the screen clearly.

steps.instruction: Push lint screen firmly back in
details: Push until it sits flat and snug.
steps.check: The screen sits flat in its slot.

steps.instruction: Take out half the load
details: Clothes need room to tumble.
Dry towels separately from light clothes.
steps.check: The drum is only about half to three-quarters full.

steps.instruction: Run a short timed dry, feel the vent
details: Set Timed Dry for 10 minutes and press Start.
Go outside and hold your hand under the vent hood.
Air should feel strong and warm, like a hair dryer.
steps.check: Strong warm air blows out and the vent flap opens.

symptoms: I press start and nothing happens
The dryer won't turn on at all
It just beeps and won't go

plan.diagnosis: Usually the door is not latched, no cycle is chosen, or the start button was only tapped. A tripped home breaker can also stop it.
safety: Do not reach inside the dryer while the drum is moving.
If both breakers keep tripping, call an electrician.

steps.instruction: Push door firmly until it clicks
details: Move any clothes blocking the latch.
steps.check: The door stays shut when you let go.

steps.instruction: Turn cycle knob to Normal
details: The dryer will not start with no cycle chosen.
steps.check: The knob points to a drying cycle.

steps.instruction: Press the power button once
details: Look for lights on the control panel.
steps.check: Control panel lights turn on.

steps.instruction: Hold start button for one second
details: Hold until the status lights come on, then let go.
A quick tap may not start it.
steps.check: The drum starts turning.

steps.instruction: Check power plug is pushed in
details: The plug is behind the dryer.
Do not pull the dryer out by its door.
steps.check: The plug sits tight in the outlet.

steps.instruction: Turn both dryer breakers off, then on
details: This dryer uses two breakers.
They are in your home breaker box.
steps.check: Both breakers are switched fully on.

symptoms: The drum turns but the clothes stay cold
It runs but there's no heat at all
Clothes come out cold and wet

plan.diagnosis: The Air Only cycle makes no heat by design, so check that first. If a heated cycle is chosen, one of the two home breakers may have tripped.
safety: Unplug the dryer before checking anything behind it.
If it still makes no heat on a heated cycle, book a service visit.

steps.instruction: Turn cycle knob to Timed Dry
details: Do not use Air Only. It never heats.
steps.check: The knob points to Timed Dry, not Air Only.

steps.instruction: Press temperature button to Medium
details: Medium is a safe heated choice for most clothes.
steps.check: The Medium temperature light is on.

steps.instruction: Hold start button for one second
details: Let the empty dryer run for 5 minutes.
steps.check: The dryer runs with the door closed.

steps.instruction: Open door and feel inside drum
details: Feel the air and the drum wall.
It should feel warm after 5 minutes.
steps.check: The inside of the drum feels warm.

steps.instruction: Turn both dryer breakers off, then on
details: One breaker runs the drum, the other runs the heat.
Both must be on for heat.
steps.check: Both breakers are switched fully on.

steps.instruction: Pull the lint screen straight up
details: Clean it, then push it firmly back in.
A blocked screen can cause long, cool drying.
steps.check: The clean screen is back in place.

problems.cause: the wrong cycle or a tripped breaker

symptoms: It turns off and my clothes are still damp
The cycle ends way too early
Small loads never get dry

plan.diagnosis: Sensor cycles stop when the metal sensor strips think clothes are dry. Very small loads may not touch the strips, and dryer-sheet coating on the strips can fool them.
safety: Unplug the dryer before wiping inside the drum.
Do not use anything sharp on the sensor strips.

steps.instruction: Unplug the dryer power plug
details: Pull the plug from the wall outlet.
steps.check: The plug is out of the outlet.

steps.instruction: Open door and find sensor strips
details: Two shiny metal strips just inside the drum.
Look near the door opening.
steps.check: You can see two shiny metal strips.

steps.instruction: Wipe sensor strips with soft cloth
details: Use a dry or slightly damp soft cloth.
Wipe away any white or waxy coating.
steps.check: The strips look clean and shiny.

steps.instruction: Plug the dryer back in
details: Push the plug firmly into the outlet.
steps.check: The plug sits tight in the outlet.

steps.instruction: Turn cycle knob to Timed Dry
details: Use Timed Dry for very small loads.
Small loads may not touch the sensor strips.
steps.check: The knob points to Timed Dry.

steps.instruction: Hold start button for one second
details: Check clothes when the cycle ends.
steps.check: The dryer starts and keeps running.

symptoms: It thumps over and over
The dryer shakes and makes a banging noise
It's much louder than it used to be

plan.diagnosis: Sheets and blankets often roll into a tight ball that thumps as it tumbles. A dryer that is not level, or a missing foot, can also rock and knock.
safety: Stop the dryer before reaching inside.
Ask another adult to help if the dryer must be moved.

steps.instruction: Press start button to pause dryer
details: Wait until the drum stops turning.
steps.check: The drum has stopped.

steps.instruction: Open door and untangle the load
details: Shake out sheets and blankets loosely.
Take out shoes. They thump loudly.
steps.check: Clothes are loose, not in a tight ball.

steps.instruction: Push door firmly until it clicks
details: Make sure no clothes block the latch.
steps.check: The door stays shut.

steps.instruction: Rock dryer gently corner to corner
details: It should not wobble.
All four feet should touch the floor.
steps.check: The dryer does not rock.

steps.instruction: Twist the wobbly foot down
details: Turn it until it touches the floor firmly.
Check front feet at the bottom front corners.
steps.check: All four feet touch the floor and the dryer is steady.

steps.instruction: Hold start button for one second
details: Listen for the first minute.
A light thump after long non-use should fade.
steps.check: The dryer runs without steady thumping.

symptoms: The light inside the dryer is out
It's dark inside the drum
The bulb inside doesn't come on

plan.diagnosis: The small bulb inside the drum has likely burned out. The manual shows how to change it with a new 10 W appliance bulb.
tools: 1/4 inch nut driver or socket wrench
safety: Unplug the dryer before changing the bulb.
Let a hot old bulb cool before touching it.
Use a 10 W appliance bulb only.

steps.instruction: Unplug the dryer power plug
details: Pull the plug from the wall outlet.
steps.check: The plug is out of the outlet.

steps.instruction: Open door and find light cover
details: It is on the back wall inside the drum.
steps.check: You can see the small light cover.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the light cover screw
details: Use a 1/4 inch nut driver or socket wrench.
The screw is at the lower right of the cover.
steps.check: The cover comes off in your hand.

steps.instruction: Twist old bulb left and out
details: Twist counterclockwise gently.
If it is stuck, wait until it is fully cool.
steps.check: The old bulb is out.

steps.instruction: Screw new bulb in gently
details: Use a 10 W appliance bulb only.
Turn clockwise until snug. Do not force it.
steps.check: The new bulb sits firm and straight.

steps.instruction: Screw light cover back on
details: Put the cover back, then tighten its screw.
steps.check: The cover is secure.

steps.instruction: Plug the dryer back in
details: Open the door to check the light.
steps.check: The drum light comes on when the door opens.

symptoms: Clothes come out all wrinkled
I left a load sitting and now it's creased
Everything looks crushed when I open the door

plan.diagnosis: Wrinkles set when a finished load sits still in a warm drum. The Wrinkle Shield option keeps tumbling the load, and Steam Refresh can relax wrinkles in dry clothes.
safety: Do not dry items with foam, rubber, or plastic on a heated cycle.
Check clothing labels before using heat.

steps.instruction: Shake each item out by hand
details: Give shirts and pants a good snap shake.
steps.check: Clothes are loose and shaken out.

steps.instruction: Turn cycle knob to Steam Refresh
details: Use for dry, wrinkled clothes only.
Do not add dryer sheets.
steps.check: The knob points to Steam Refresh.

steps.instruction: Press options button once
details: One press turns on Wrinkle Shield.
It tumbles the load on and off after the cycle.
steps.check: The Wrinkle Shield light is on.

steps.instruction: Push door firmly until it clicks
details: Make sure no clothes block the latch.
steps.check: The door stays shut.

steps.instruction: Hold start button for one second
details: Hold until the status lights come on, then let go.
steps.check: The dryer starts tumbling.

steps.instruction: Take clothes out when cycle ends
details: Hang or fold them right away.
This stops new wrinkles setting in.
steps.check: Clothes are out and hung or folded.

symptoms: Clothes are still damp even with a clean lint screen
The outside vent barely blows any air
The top of the dryer gets very hot

plan.diagnosis: With a clean lint screen, the next most likely cause is lint packed in the vent hose or the outside flap. The hot, wet air can't get out, so the dryer runs long and hot.
tools: Vent brush or a vacuum hose
replacement_parts: New 4-inch foil or semi-rigid vent hose, only if yours is torn or crushed
safety: Unplug the dryer before you pull it out.
If the vent goes up through the roof or you can't reach it, call a dryer vent cleaning service.

steps.instruction: Unplug the dryer from the wall
details: The plug is behind the dryer, low on the wall.
steps.check: The plug is out of the outlet.

steps.instruction: Pull the dryer out about two feet
details: Slide it straight out so the hose doesn't tear.
steps.check: There is room to reach behind the dryer.

steps.instruction: Loosen the clamp and pull the hose off
details: The silver hose fits over a round pipe on the back.
Loosen the clamp with a screwdriver, then twist and pull.
steps.target_part: silver vent hose on the back
steps.check: The hose is off the round pipe.

steps.instruction: Pull the lint out of the hose and pipe
details: Reach in by hand, then use a vent brush or a vacuum.
Clean the round pipe on the dryer's back too.
steps.check: No lint inside the hose or the pipe.

steps.instruction: Check the outside vent flap swings open
details: Go outside and find the vent hood on the wall.
Clear lint, nests or snow so the flap moves freely.
steps.check: The flap opens and closes freely.

steps.instruction: Push the hose back on and tighten the clamp
details: Slide the dryer back slowly so the hose stays round, not crushed.
steps.target_part: silver vent hose on the back
steps.check: The hose is on, clamped and not squashed.

steps.instruction: Plug in, run a short timed dry, feel the vent
details: Run Timed Dry on high for 10 minutes.
Outside, you should feel strong, warm air.
steps.check: Strong warm air comes out of the outside vent.

plan.aftercare: Clean the vent hose once a year, and the lint screen every load.

symptoms: It tumbles but never gets warm, even with a clean vent
No heat at all after the vent was blocked

plan.diagnosis: If the vent is clear and it still won't heat, a thermal fuse has probably blown (a blocked vent often causes this) or the heating element has burned out. Both sit behind the back panel, so this is a part swap for a pro.
replacement_parts: Thermal fuse for your model (match it by the model number)
Heating element for your model, if the fuse isn't it
safety: The fix means opening the back panel near 240-volt wiring, so leave it to a pro unless you're trained.
Keep the dryer unplugged until it's fixed.

steps.instruction: Unplug the dryer
details: The plug is behind the dryer, low on the wall.
steps.check: The plug is out of the outlet.

steps.instruction: Find the model number inside the door
details: Open the door and look around the edge of the opening.
Take a photo of the sticker.
steps.target_part: model sticker on the door frame
steps.check: You have a photo of the model sticker.

steps.instruction: Call a pro, or order the part for your model
details: Tell them what you already tried, so you don't pay for the same checks.
A parts store can match the part to your model number.

steps.instruction: After the repair, test for heat
details: Run Timed Dry on high for 5 minutes.
The drum and clothes should feel warm.
steps.check: The drum feels warm.

plan.aftercare: Keep the vent clean so the new fuse doesn't blow again.

problems.cause: a blown thermal fuse or heating element

parts.label: Water inlet hose — steam models (behind dryer)
